title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Ethan Park
description:
Motivation:
We observed periodic tail-latency regressions and request starvation on high-concurrency mixed workloads. The continuous batcher scheduler was prioritizing throughput at the expense of fairness across queues, and soft timeouts meant some requests would be indefinitely postponed under sustained load. This PR tunes the scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add explicit starvation detection and prevention, and introduce configurable soft/hard timeouts with graceful requeueing logic.

What this PR changes (high level):
- Introduces per-queue fair-share weights and a token-based queueing window to balance throughput and fairness.
- Adds starvation detector that identifies queues that have been skipped beyond a configurable threshold and forces a high-priority drain for a limited number of batches.
- Implements soft and hard timeout semantics: soft timeout triggers best-effort requeue with exponential backoff, hard timeout returns early-failure to caller after metrics/logging.
- Adds metrics and traces around queue wait-time, starvation events, preemption counts, and timeout rates.
- Provides new scheduler knobs (env/config): scheduler.queue_window_ms, scheduler.queue_weights, scheduler.starvation_threshold_ms, scheduler.soft_timeout_ms, scheduler.hard_timeout_ms, scheduler.max_preemptions.

Performance and correctness summary:
- Tail latency (p99) for mixed small/large batch workload reduced by ~9% in our canary runs.
- Median latency unchanged; throughput sustained within 1-2% of baseline.
- Starvation cases observed in replayed customer traces were eliminated (0 occurrences vs ~18 in baseline) with starvation_threshold_ms=500ms and max_preemptions=3.
- Unit + integration tests added; benchmark harness scenarios updated to include starvation trace replays.

Files changed (high-level):
- src/serving/continuous_batcher/scheduler.cpp: core scheduler loop and token window logic.
- src/serving/continuous_batcher/scheduler.h: new config knobs and API for preemption/starvation.
- src/serving/continuous_batcher/starvation_detector.cpp/h: detector and mitigation logic.
- src/serving/continuous_batcher/timeout_policy.cpp: soft/hard timeout handling and backoff.
- test/continuous_batcher/scheduler_integration_test.cc: new tests for fairness and starvation.
- bench/continuous_batcher/mixed_workload_bench.py: updated scenarios and measurement harness.
- docs/ops/scheduler-tuning.md: operational notes and recommended knob values.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- All new knobs are opt-in via config; defaults set to conservative values to avoid regressions.
- Plan: merge to main, run extended canaries on staging (2 days), then rollout to canary fleet. If regressions observed, feature flags allow disabling new starvation mitigation and timeouts per deployment.

Checklist:
- [x] Code changes + unit tests
- [x] Integration tests for starvation cases
- [x] Benchmarks updated and run against replay traces
- [x] Docs updated with operational guidance
- [x] Reviewed and approved by runtime and SRE

Notes:
- This PR intentionally keeps preemption conservative (default max_preemptions=3) to avoid thrashing. We can iterate on defaults after observing canary behavior.
- Follow-up PR will expose queue-level telemetry in the Console UI for detailed per-queue wait distributions.

release_notes:
- Improve continuous-batcher scheduler fairness via per-queue weights and tokenized queue window.
- Add starvation detection and limited preemption to guarantee forward progress for starved queues.
- Introduce soft/hard timeouts with requeue/backoff behavior and new metrics for monitoring.
